data.narrative:
Collaborative Robotics, founded by Brad Porter, is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—alongside one public comparable and eight additional private references across the broader robotics ecosystem.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach, anchored to a $500M last post-money valuation, applies a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, yielding $950M. The peer-median method references the three identified comps, which trade at a median valuation of $1.8B (range: $1.6B–$2.0B). These methods triangulate to a low of $808M, median of $1.4B, and high of $2.0B.

The median estimate of $1.4B sits between the stage-progression floor ($950M) and peer median ceiling ($1.8B), reflecting tension between earlier-stage comparable growth patterns and current peer market pricing. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-company peer set—which, while same-stage and sector-aligned, may not fully capture Collaborative Robotics' specific unit economics or capital efficiency—and the stability of peer valuations in an inherently cyclical manufacturing technology market. The $808M–$2.0B range reflects these data constraints.
